label: The stance cannot meet its demand for reasons why and accept the fact as a brute contingent truth
paraphrase: Conclusion of the parity argument: in any picture and at any world, the stance does not at once meet its demand for reasons why, accept the fact o, and have o a contingent truth with no reason there. For o the existence of the contingent foundation, the stance cannot hold the brute-contingency rival. It is a consistency verdict on the stance; it does not say o has a reason, and it does not establish B2. For a necessary o (God's existence, a necessary base) it holds vacuously, since BruteAt requires contingency; the stronger sibling without contingency is what binds acceptance of an unreasoned necessary existent.
